newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian Moslem leader calls for liquor ban.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian Moslem leader calls for liquor ban.

text.p: The leader of a powerful group of Indonesian Moslem scholars has called for a ban on liquor following government measures to control distribution, the official Antara news agency said on Monday.
"In my opinion, I stress that alcoholic drinks should be banned in Indonesia," Hasan Basri, leader of the Council of Ulemas (MUI), was quoted by Antara as saying.

Hasan said that only after a ban was imposed could the possibility of selling liquor under controlled conditions be considered. Factors such as where the alcohol was sold and to whom were important, he said.
Moslems were enraged this month by a revision in liquor laws proposed by the Jakarta municipal government which aimed to increase levies on liquor and to control distribution in the city.
The bill, already passed by parliament, is now before the Home Ministry.
Moslem groups said the move would raise money for the government from undesirable sources and would give social sanction to liquor in a mainly Islamic society.
Indonesia's population of 190 million is 85 percent Moslem, although alcohol is freely available in most areas.
